drip.author: goalie_mom_deb
drip.title: First 6 a.m. ice time of the season, and the quiet dad in the stands brought a second coffee for me
drip.body:
Every September, first early ice time, the canteen isn't open yet and I've forgotten to stop for coffee. Eleven years running. It's practically tradition: me in the cold stands with my scarf pulled up, muttering about it.

There's a dad whose kid has been at the same rink as my son for two seasons, and we've exchanged maybe twenty words in that time. This morning he sat down one row ahead with two drive-through cups, passed one back to me and said "figured." That was it. That was the entire conversation. He watched the rest of the session like nothing had happened.

It was honestly not very good coffee. Best coffee I've had all year.

comments.author: twoferone
comments.body: "Figured" is a full paragraph in dad. It means: I noticed you, I planned for you, please don't make this weird.

comments.author: quietkettle
comments.body: The kindest people often manage it in the fewest words. He ordered an extra cup at a drive-through before dawn on the chance you'd forget. That's a little piece of his morning spent thinking about someone else.

replies.author: goalie_mom_deb
replies.body: I'm bringing him a coffee next week. Good coffee. He is going to hate the fuss and I'm doing it anyway.

comments.author: thrifted_thunder
comments.body: Two seasons, twenty words, one extra coffee. That's how the best rink friendships start. By next year he'll say "morning" and you'll both know it means a lot.

comments.author: offsidewinger
comments.body: Beer league guy here. The stands at a 6 a.m. rink are held together by exactly this kind of person. Nobody talks, everybody notices.

drip.author: twoferone
drip.title: My twins named the crossing guard's stop sign. She has fully committed to the bit
drip.body:
First week of school, the twins decided the crossing guard's stop sign looked lonely and needed a name. They landed on Stanley. Why Stanley? "He looks like a Stanley." He is a sign.

She could have laughed it off. Instead, every morning since, she holds him up and announces "Stanley says wait" and "Stanley says go." This week a kindergartner with a dinosaur backpack waved goodbye to Stanley. The sign has fans. The sign has a morning routine.

My boys now walk to that corner like they're about to meet a celebrity. She's out there in the cold every single day, and somehow she's the one making their morning.

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: Crossing guards are the unsung heroes of September. Standing in the cold being cheerful for a hundred sleepy kids, and she still found the energy to give a sign a personality. Somebody get that woman a warm drink.

comments.author: second_act_sylvia
comments.body: The best adults are the ones who say yes to a kid's idea instead of explaining why it's silly. She could have said "it's just a sign." She gave Stanley a job title instead.

comments.author: solsticegrower
comments.body: A kindergartner waving goodbye to Stanley is going to be in my head all day, in the best way.

replies.author: twoferone
replies.body: This morning one of the twins asked if Stanley gets summers off. I said yes. He said "good, Stanley works hard." They are very protective of that sign.

comments.author: twelve_rescues_later
comments.body: Stanley is now the most important institution on your street and I will hear no arguments.

drip.author: solsticegrower
drip.title: Let the neighbour kids help dig the potatoes. One of them adopted a potato
drip.body:
Potato harvest this weekend, and the two kids next door asked if they could help. I handed them trowels expecting ten minutes of interest. They dug for two hours. Every potato got held up to the sky like buried treasure. The little one kept count out loud and lost track somewhere around "a lot plus six."

Then she found one shaped almost exactly like a duck and refused to put it in the bucket. It went home with her. Her dad texted me a photo this morning: the duck potato is on her windowsill with googly eyes and a paper crown. I've grown a lot of potatoes, and none of them ever went to a better home.

comments.author: quietkettle
comments.body: "A lot plus six" is the correct number of potatoes for any good harvest. And you gave her two hours of the best kind of work, the kind where you can see exactly what you did.

comments.author: twelve_rescues_later
comments.body: Gentle warning from someone who has fostered a lot of living things: that potato is going to sprout in a sunny window. Tell her it's not a bad sign, it's the potato settling in.

replies.author: solsticegrower
replies.body: Already warned her dad. The plan is to plant the duck in the spring and find out whether it has ducklings. I think I've recruited a gardener.

comments.author: thrifted_thunder
comments.body: Two hours of labour paid entirely in potatoes and one duck. Best deal on the whole street, and everybody walked away richer.

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: Mine would have done the exact same thing with a rock. It's never really about the potato. It's about a grown-up letting you keep the weird one.

drip.author: thrifted_thunder
drip.title: Watched the worst driveway negotiation of my life at a yard sale last weekend. It was perfect
drip.body:
One of the last good yard sale weekends of the year, so I ran my full route. At one driveway an older gentleman was selling off an entire sewing room: fabric, thread, patterns, and a machine that probably weighs more than I do. It was his wife's, he said.

A teenager picked up a pincushion and mentioned she was teaching herself to sew from videos. He asked what machine she used. She didn't have one, she'd been doing everything by hand. He peeled the price sticker off the machine, gave it to her, and would not take a dollar. Then he spent twenty minutes in a lawn chair showing her how to thread it while her mom and I pretended to be very interested in some teacups.

I have haggled on a lot of driveways. That was the worst deal I've ever seen anyone make, and the best trade I've ever watched.

comments.author: second_act_sylvia
comments.body: He wasn't selling a machine. He was waiting for the right person to take it, and he knew the second she said "by hand."

comments.author: quietkettle
comments.body: Twenty minutes in a lawn chair teaching someone to thread a needle. That was the real gift. The machine is just what it came in.

replies.author: thrifted_thunder
replies.body: Her mom and I compared notes after. Neither of us bought a teacup, and neither of us could tell you what the teacups looked like.

comments.author: twoferone
comments.body: You two pretending to shop for teacups while that happened is its own kind of kindness. You let them have it without an audience.

comments.author: OttomanEmpire
comments.body: Upholsterer here. A home machine that heavy is usually metal all the way through and will outlast everyone in this story. She's got a machine for life, and he got to watch it go to someone who'll actually use it.

drip.author: second_act_sylvia
drip.title: Showed my neighbour how to send a photo from his phone. Now I get the sky every morning
drip.body:
My neighbour is 78 and got a new phone from his grandkids that he mostly used as a very expensive clock. Last month he knocked on my door and asked if I'd show him how to send a picture. It took about ten minutes, most of which was finding the camera.

The next morning at 6:52, a photo of the sky over the houses across the street. No caption. The morning after, same thing, a little foggier. Every day since. Clouds, a sunrise, one very blurry crow. The sun is coming up later now, so the photos arrive later too, and I've started waking up a few minutes before the text comes in.

I've never asked him why. I don't think I need to know. I just want tomorrow's.

comments.author: solsticegrower
comments.body: Watching sunrise slide a little later every day through someone else's photos is a lovely way to feel the season turn. You two are keeping a sky diary together without ever calling it that.

comments.author: twelve_rescues_later
comments.body: The blurry crow is my favourite and I haven't even seen it.

replies.author: second_act_sylvia
replies.body: It is genuinely the best one. It's mostly thumb. The crow is implied.

comments.author: goalie_mom_deb
comments.body: There's an older fellow at our rink who uses his phone as a clock too. I think I know what I'm doing between periods this week. Thank you for the ten minutes you didn't have to give, and for passing it on.

comments.author: quietkettle
comments.body: Some people text good morning. He sends you the actual morning. That's better.

late_comments.author: twelve_rescues_later
late_comments.body: Found this looking up how to glue a garden ornament and ended up not needing the instructions. A foster kitten knocked the ceramic frog off my front step this week and it now has a crack straight through its smile. I'm leaving it exactly like that. This thread ruined me for perfect lawn ornaments.

late_comments.author: quietkettle
late_comments.body: This one came back to me at the library book sale last weekend. I was a dollar short at the library book sale last weekend, and the teenager at the table just said "that one looks like it wants to go with you." I put two dollars in the donation jar on my way out. It does keep going.
